headline: The US National Institute on Aging has awarded Hello Robot nearly three million dollars to test its Stretch robot as a helper for older adults with early memory loss.
score_reason: Funded research in elder care; early-stage and years from a product.
importance_line: Older adults with mild cognitive impairment and their carers are the intended users, but this is a three-year research study, not a product.
summary: Robotics & Automation News reports that Hello Robot, a US maker of the Stretch mobile manipulator robot, has been awarded a grant of nearly $3 million over three years from the National Institute on Aging, part of the National Institutes of Health. With the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, it will test how Stretch can help older adults with mild memory loss at home and in care settings; the project began on 22 Sep 2026 and runs to May 2029.
notes: Based on a project announcement with company quotes; the grant start of 22 Sep is earlier than the report but the announcement is new.
